I migrated `src/module.ts` to es-toolkit and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks (under `--strict --skipLibCheck`) and bundles at 242 bytes min+gzip, of which 95 bytes are my own code. I didn't run the migrated functions against the original on the example inputs; I only reasoned about equivalence.

I could not measure the original: `npm run size -- src/module.ts` fails because `lodash` isn't installed here. So I have no baseline to compare the 95 bytes of own code against.

The type check needed `--skipLibCheck`. Without it, tsc reports two errors inside es-toolkit's own declarations (`Disposable` and `AsyncDisposable` not found), which have nothing to do with my file.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mapValues(obj, fn)` | `mapValues` | Same call shape. |
| `keyBy(rows, 'name')` | `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)` | es-toolkit's `keyBy` takes a function, not a property name, so this is the small adapter you allowed. |
| `sortedUniq(values)` | `uniq(values)` | es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. On sorted input `uniq` gives the same result, and your input range guarantees sorted arrays. |

- **`uniq` vs `sortedUniq`:** `uniq` doesn't assume the input is sorted, so it behaves differently from `sortedUniq` on unsorted arrays.
- **No lodash left:** I kept no lodash import, and the exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged.

The import now reads `import { mapValues, keyBy, uniq } from 'es-toolkit';`.
